prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor bouldering wall directly in front of the camera wearer in frames 1–3 and a wide blue floor mat below in frames 4–5 as the camera turns away from the wall and looks down. In frames 1 and 2, the wall surface, triangular volumes, and holds are within arm's reach at roughly 0.3–1.0 m, while the wearer's own hands, bent right leg below, and another climber slightly below and to the right are visible at 0.2–1.5 m; in frame 3, the wearer's raised left arm is extremely close (under 0.3 m, bright white) in the left foreground, partially occluding the blue floor mat roughly 2–3 m below. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer drops or moves toward the mat while turning toward five people standing 2–5 m away near the base of the wall, separated from each other by about 0.5–1.5 m, with one person in a dark shirt approaching from roughly 3.5 m in frame 4 to about 2 m in frame 5 while extending their right hand toward the wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient makes the steep drop-off from the climbing wall to the floor in frame 3 and the continuous slope of the mat relative to the standing figures in frames 4–5 much clearer. However, the map is unreliable around the fine contours of small climbing holds in frame 2, which blur into the wall plane, and along the dark background behind the bystanders in frames 4–5 where the lower wall and floor transition lose geometric detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground regions across the scene, though most of the climbing wall and main floor mat remain unsegmented black background. In frames 1–3, it outlines parts of the camera wearer's limbs within 0.2–0.8 m (bottom center/left) and an adjacent person on the lower right (about 1–1.5 m away), while in frames 4 and 5 it separates the people standing along the top edge 2–5 m away (spaced 0.5–1.5 m apart, with their upper bodies or heads partly cropped out of the top of the frame) and a rectangular crash pad lying on the left side of the floor about 3 m away. Across frames 4 and 5, the masks show the central person in the dark shirt stepping forward from the line of three people on the right to roughly 2 m in front of the camera wearer, while a person in a white shirt remains to the far left within arm's reach of the small crash pad. While segmentation clearly delineates the boundaries of the cropped bystanders' legs at the top of frames 4–5 and separates overlapping limbs in frame 1 better than a quick glance at RGB, its semantic labels and masks are highly unreliable during the close-up wall views. Specifically, it misclassifies triangular climbing volumes and the floor mat pad as 'surfboard' and 'skateboard', labels orange climbing holds as 'carrot' or 'person', and merges the camera wearer's arm with the entire lower wall and mat into a single 'person' mask in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1–4 and detects only a single body and hand skeleton in the upper-middle region of frame 5. In frame 5, this yellow torso-and-leg skeleton corresponds to the approaching person in the dark shirt standing roughly 2 m in front of and slightly below the camera wearer, facing directly toward the camera with their head cropped out above the top edge of the frame. The skeleton shows their left arm hanging down by their left hip and their right arm raised and extended forward toward the left side of the image, placing their detailed magenta right-hand skeleton within about 1.5 m of the camera wearer. This explicit skeletal wireframe makes the exact joint angles of the approaching person's forward stride, torso orientation, and open right-hand finger splay easier to read than in the dark clothing of the RGB frame. However, the pose map is unreliable across the sequence because it fails to detect the camera wearer's own visible arms and legs within 0.2–0.8 m in frames 1–3, misses the adjacent climber on the right in frames 1–2, and misses all other partially cropped standing people 2.5–5 m away in frames 4 and 5.
